prompt: Which 2 stores sold the most units per order line in 2025? Use the sales table and keep the order lines with an order_date from 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, both included. Return two columns, in this order: store_code and units_per_line, the total of units divided by the number of order lines, with all its decimals kept. Count every order line, including a line whose units value is missing: a missing units value adds nothing to the total. Sort by units_per_line from highest to lowest, and when two stores have the same units_per_line, by store_code from A to Z. Return only the first 2 rows, one row per store_code. Do not round.
hints: Next, keep the 2025 lines, decide what one row stands for, write units_per_line, then write the sort and the row limit.

Both the total of units and the count of lines are whole numbers, so make one side a decimal before you divide; integer division would make many stores tie. Put the store_code tie-break after units_per_line in the same ORDER BY, from A to Z.
why_this_works: A decimal division keeps the small differences between stores, and the store_code tie-break settles which of two equal values comes first at the cut-off.
